title: The CI release workflow has the same ungated wrapper publish that QCLI-299 fixed locally
description:
Found while fixing QCLI-299, in a file its acceptance criteria do not name, so it is filed rather than folded in.

QCLI-299 gates the WRAPPER publish on a consumer-side read of all six platform packages, but only in scripts/publish-release.mjs. The CI path has the identical defect: .github/workflows/release.yml publishes the six platform packages in a shell loop and then publishes @opum-ai/quest immediately after, with nothing between them but the loop ending. The retry step that follows is the same confirmation-not-gate shape QCLI-299 removed from the local script -- it runs AFTER the wrapper is already on the registry.

Not urgent, and the reason is worth stating rather than assuming: this path did not publish 0.7.0. Trusted publishing is still broken (QCLI-271, an immutable-subject-claim mismatch in the OIDC exchange), so releases are going out through the local script, which is the path that now has the gate. The day CI publishing is restored is the day this defect becomes live again, and that is exactly when nobody will be looking at it.

The fix is not a copy of the script: CI runs the loop in shell, so the gate belongs as a step between the platform loop and the wrapper publish, invoking the same waitForConsumerVisibility used locally rather than reimplementing the read.

acceptanceCriteria.text: release.yml does not publish @opum-ai/quest until a consumer-side read confirms all six platform packages resolve, using scripts/qualification/registry-visibility.mjs rather than a second implementation of the same read
A failed gate fails the job with the per-package state printed, and leaves the wrapper unpublished -- verified by a dry-run or fixture, not by reasoning about the YAML
The post-publish retry step stays, and its message no longer claims a timeout is lag rather than a failed release
The relationship to QCLI-271 is recorded: if trusted publishing is restored before this lands, that restoration is what makes this defect live

implementationNotes:
Implemented as a gate STEP between the platform loop and the wrapper publish, per the task own direction not to copy the local script: CI runs the loop in shell, so the fix is a step invoking the same read, not a reimplementation.

scripts/qualification/require-platform-visibility.mjs is a thin runner over registry-visibility.mjs (waitForConsumerVisibility, classifyVersion, describeVersionState). Deliberately thin: two implementations of "did it land" would drift, and the CI one is the one nobody runs by hand.

release.yml restructured: "Publish" renamed to "Publish the platform packages" (loop only), then the gate step, then a separate "Publish the wrapper" step. The gate is skipped on a dry run because nothing was published to become visible -- asserting otherwise would fail every dry run for the right reason at the wrong time.

AC 3: the propagation step stays, and its timeout message no longer diagnoses the cause. It previously asserted "npm-side CDN/attestation-processing lag". With the gate upstream, platform-package lag is the one explanation now RULED OUT -- the gate already confirmed a consumer-side read of all six. What remains is most likely the wrapper never landing, or a package that resolved for the gate ceasing to resolve, which is the CDN serving two documents and is a real fault rather than a slow one. The message now says so and says to treat the release as incomplete.

Verification is a fixture, not YAML reasoning, as AC 2 requires: requirePlatformVisibility takes injected wait/classify, so the refusal path runs with no network. Five tests. The ordering assertion was mutation-tested -- moving the gate to AFTER the wrapper publish reddens exactly that test and leaves the other four green, so it detects the precise defect QCLI-300 describes rather than merely reading the file.

Two things typecheck caught that reasoning had not: the fixtures were too loose, and VersionState has no "absent" member -- the correct value is "absent-or-staged", because from a consumer read those two are genuinely indistinguishable. Collapsing them in a fixture would have modelled a distinction the report exists to preserve.

bun run check exits 0, 566 tests across 66 files.

AC 4, the QCLI-271 relationship, recorded here because it is the part most likely to be lost:

This defect is currently DORMANT, not fixed-and-therefore-safe. The CI publish path did not publish 0.7.0 or 0.7.1. Trusted publishing is still broken (QCLI-271: an immutable-subject-claim mismatch in the OIDC exchange), so releases go out through scripts/publish-release.mjs, which is the path QCLI-299 already gated. THE DAY QCLI-271 IS RESOLVED AND CI PUBLISHING IS RESTORED IS THE DAY THIS DEFECT WOULD HAVE BECOME LIVE -- and that is precisely the day nobody would have been looking at it, because restoring trusted publishing reads as unrelated infrastructure work.

That ordering is the whole reason this was worth doing ahead of need rather than when CI publishing returns. Anyone working QCLI-271 should know the gate is already in place and does not need to be remembered.

AC 2 evidence, stated with its limitation rather than implied:
- Hermetic, in the suite: requirePlatformVisibility with injected wait/classify returns ok:false, prints THE WRAPPER WAS NOT PUBLISHED, names the unresolved package, and never logs the success line. Plus an ordering assertion over release.yml, mutation-tested -- moving the gate after the wrapper publish reddens exactly that test and leaves the other four green.
- End to end, measured by hand and NOT added as a test: `node scripts/qualification/require-platform-visibility.mjs 9.9.9 --max-wait-ms 1 --registry http://127.0.0.1:9` exits 1 with the full per-package report. It is not in the suite because classifyVersion shells out to `npm stage list` to separate staged from never-landed, so it needs network and a credential and would be flaky in CI for reasons unrelated to this gate. parseArgs is unit-tested instead, so a typo in a flag name cannot silently restore the 15-minute default.

What this does NOT prove, and should not be read as proving: that a failing step halts the job and leaves the wrapper unpublished is GitHub Actions step semantics, asserted through the ordering test plus the workflow contract, not executed here. The first real CI publish after QCLI-271 is the first time that half runs for real.
finalSummary:
CI no longer publishes the wrapper before its platform packages are consumer-visible. QCLI-299 established that rule and fixed only scripts/publish-release.mjs; .github/workflows/release.yml carried the identical defect -- a shell loop publishing six platform packages, then @opum-ai/quest on the very next line, with the propagation loop running AFTER the wrapper was already on the registry, which makes it a confirmation rather than a gate.

Fixed as the task directed rather than by copying the local script: the loop stays in shell, and a gate STEP sits between it and a new separate wrapper-publish step. scripts/qualification/require-platform-visibility.mjs is a deliberately thin runner over registry-visibility.mjs, because two implementations of "did it land" would drift and the CI one is the one nobody runs by hand. Skipped on dry runs, where nothing was published to become visible.

AC 3: the propagation step stays and its timeout message no longer diagnoses the cause. It previously asserted npm-side CDN lag. With the gate upstream, platform-package lag is the one explanation now ruled out, so the message says not to assume lag, names what actually remains (the wrapper never landing, or a package that resolved for the gate ceasing to resolve -- the CDN serving two documents, a real fault rather than a slow one), and says to treat the release as incomplete.

Verified: 568 tests, bun run check exits 0. The refusal is demonstrated by fixture with injected wait/classify, and the ordering assertion is mutation-tested -- moving the gate after the wrapper publish reddens exactly that test and leaves the other four green, so it detects the precise defect rather than merely reading the file. End to end, the runner exits 1 with the full per-package report against a registry that resolves nothing; that invocation is recorded in the notes rather than added to the suite, because it shells out to npm stage list and would be flaky in CI for unrelated reasons.

Stated rather than implied: this defect is DORMANT, not made safe. The CI path published neither 0.7.0 nor 0.7.1, because trusted publishing is still broken (QCLI-271). Restoring it is what would have made this live, on a day nobody would have been looking. Anyone working QCLI-271 should know the gate is already there. Equally, that a failing step halts the job is GitHub Actions semantics asserted through the ordering test and the workflow contract, not executed here -- the first real CI publish after QCLI-271 is the first time that half runs for real.

Two corrections typecheck made that reasoning had not: the fixtures were too loose, and VersionState has no "absent" member -- it is "absent-or-staged", because from a consumer read those are genuinely indistinguishable, a distinction the report exists to preserve.
